newsitem.title: USA: US spot butane up on tight MTBE supply, cargo talk.
newsitem.headline: US spot butane up on tight MTBE supply, cargo talk.

text.p: U.S. spot normal butane prices rose in midday trade on Friday amid tight supplies of gasoline additive MTBE and rumors a large cargo of butane is about to be sold.

Traders said that a 20,000-tonne cargo of normal butane was heard being negotiated for sale by Venezuela to possibly Mexico. It was unclear if the material would then be shipped to the U.S. Gulf for storage since Mexico lacks storage space.
In the U.S. Gulf, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot normal butane was done at 41.00 cents a gallon early Friday morning, about a penny above Thursday, players said.

Traders said the sharp rise in prices of MTBE, which is made with butane, was partly behind the rise in values. MTBE has risen more than 20.00 cents in the past month as gasoline blenders fight for a shrinking pool of prompt supply.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, normal butane traded at 37.75 cents, about a quarter cent above Thursday.
The propane market was talked steady, with deals done at 34.75 cents in Belvieu. Conway material was 34.25/34.50 cents.
